denial.text: Prairie Commons Medicaid Plan denied the claim for CPT 43775 (laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy) with date of service 2026-02-16. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. Payer remark: Documentation does not demonstrate completion of the required supervised weight management program.

criteria.text: Body mass index of 40 or more, or 35 or more with at least one obesity-related comorbidity (type 2 diabetes, obstructive sleep apnea, or hypertension).
Participation in a physician-supervised weight management program for at least 6 consecutive months within the past 2 years, with monthly visits documenting diet, exercise, and weight.
Psychological evaluation finding no untreated eating disorder, substance use disorder, or psychiatric condition that would impair adherence to the postoperative regimen.
Nutrition evaluation and education on the postoperative diet completed.

chart.text: Supervised weight management visit 1 of 6. Weight 246 pounds. Reviewed the food log, 1,500 calorie plan, walking 30 minutes 5 days a week. Added a second walk on weekends.
Supervised weight management visit 2 of 6. Weight 244 pounds. Reviewed the food log, 1,500 calorie plan, walking 30 minutes 5 days a week. Struggling with evening snacking.
Supervised weight management visit 3 of 6. Weight 242 pounds. Reviewed the food log, 1,500 calorie plan, walking 30 minutes 5 days a week. Struggling with evening snacking.
Supervised weight management visit 4 of 6. Weight 240 pounds. Reviewed the food log, 1,500 calorie plan, walking 30 minutes 5 days a week. Struggling with evening snacking.
Supervised weight management visit 5 of 6. Weight 238 pounds. Reviewed the food log, 1,500 calorie plan, walking 30 minutes 5 days a week. Struggling with evening snacking.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, she will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.
From the referring physician: please evaluate and treat as you see fit. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.
Polysomnography. Apnea-hypopnea index 41 per hour, oxygen nadir 78 percent. Moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea. CPAP titrated to 11 centimeters of water.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 40. Approved 90 days. She mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.
Mammogram report forwarded for the record. Bilateral screening, BI-RADS 1, negative, routine screening in one year.

Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.
Patient called about a tick bite on the scalp after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.
Supervised weight management visit 6 of 6. Weight 236 pounds. Reviewed the food log, 1,500 calorie plan, walking 30 minutes 5 days a week. Struggling with evening snacking.

55 year old woman in bariatric surgery clinic after finishing the supervised program with her primary. Discussed sleeve versus bypass; sleeve preferred given reflux is mild and she wants the simpler operation. Her history otherwise: reflux on omeprazole as needed. Allergies: penicillin, rash. Does not smoke, a glass of wine on weekends, works in an office. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. BMI 41.5 at 5 foot 3 and 234 pounds. Type 2 diabetes on metformin with an A1c of 7.5, obstructive sleep apnea on CPAP, hypertension on two agents.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the left for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.

Pre-bariatric psychological evaluation. No binge eating disorder, no purging, no substance use, depression in remission on sertraline with a PHQ-9 of 3. Understands the lifelong dietary changes. Cleared for surgery.
Work note requested for a sick day last Monday. Faxed to the employer.

Registered dietitian evaluation. Reviewed the staged postoperative diet, protein goals of 60 to 80 grams, vitamin and mineral supplementation for life, and fluid separation from meals. Teach-back successful.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.

Twisted the right ankle stepping off a curb 3 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.
Back with the psychology and nutrition evaluations done. Reviewed the operation, the leak risk, and the postoperative diet again. Ready to schedule. Vitals today 127 over 72, pulse 85.
Nurse call. Patient had questions about time off work and whether she needs someone at home the first night. Answered both, she will arrange it.
Blood pressure check. 134 over 73 today, 143 over 88 on repeat. She has been taking the lisinopril 20 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 12 weeks.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 7 years.
She called asking about travel vaccines for a trip in early summer. Advised hepatitis A and a typhoid booster, referred to the travel clinic. Nothing else needed from us.

Called her with the cholesterol results. Total 205, LDL 144, HDL 53, triglycerides 195. Discussed diet and walking. She wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 19 and 14. No ocular pathology noted.
A1c came back 5.9. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. She is motivated.
Pre-op. Clear liquids for 2 days before, hold the metformin the morning of, CPAP to come with her. Consent signed for laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.

Mole on the right calf that her spouse noticed. About 5 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change she is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 50 denial can be answered from the record.
